title: Chapter 71: Heaven Inside the Well
html:
The afternoon sun was blinding. Even after Chen Ge firmly refused them, the woman and the boy would not leave.

“He wants to visit your Haunted House, and I promised he could. Can’t you please make an exception?” The woman pulled a hundred-RMB note from her purse. “I promise he’ll be fine.”

Chen Ge ignored the obvious bribe. “Why are you so determined to take him inside? He can’t be more than eight. The Haunted House is intense enough that it could scar him for life.”

The woman smiled helplessly but did not answer Chen Ge’s question. Instead, she turned around to rub the boy’s fluffy hair. “Fan Yu, shall we go play something else…”

Before she could finish, the boy slapped her hand away. He disliked physical contact, even from family. No matter how she coaxed him, he remained planted before the Haunted House. Whenever he raised his head, Chen Ge glimpsed fear, insecurity, and a trace of detachment in his eyes.

“Fan Yu?” The boy now held Chen Ge’s full attention. He had never encountered such a peculiar child. Squatting to eye level, he asked, “Can you tell me why you want to visit the Haunted House? It’s dark inside, and there are frightening things.”

The boy averted his eyes, though his gaze kept straying toward Chen Ge’s shadow. He said nothing.

Afraid Chen Ge might take offense, the woman hurried to explain. “Xiao Yu is different from most children. He doesn’t like to talk, so I hope you won’t mind.”

“Of course not.” They would not leave unless security removed them, and Chen Ge was not cruel enough to do that to a woman and child. At last, he relented. “How about this? I’ll let you in for free, but you may only tour the outer edge of the scenario, and I’ll stay with you the entire time.”

“Thank you!”

“First, both of you need to sign waivers. Don’t touch the props or run around inside, and stay close behind me.” Chen Ge handed forms to the woman and the boy. Ordinarily, only the guardian’s signature was required, but he asked Fan Yu to sign as well, hoping to learn as much as possible about him. Once the forms were complete, Chen Ge led them into Minghun.

Chen Ge explained the scenario’s story as they stood beneath the white lanterns at its entrance. The woman’s grip tightened around her purse, betraying her nerves. The boy kept his head down, whether from fear or something else, Chen Ge could not tell.

Dead branches swayed overhead, and paper money crunched beneath their feet. Chen Ge pushed open the entrance to the Siheyuan. “You can look inside from here, but remember, don’t enter. Park rules strictly prohibit children under fourteen from experiencing the attraction.”

Before he finished speaking, the previously silent boy darted into the Siheyuan. Neither adult reacted in time to stop him.

“Fan Yu!” The woman and Chen Ge raced after him. The boy stopped at the old well in the courtyard and leaned half his body over its rim, searching the darkness below.

“I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.” The woman apologized over and over as she tried to drag him from the well. But the timid boy seemed transformed. He fought her hands with frantic strength, clawing her arms until they bled. He had gone berserk.

Those were some violent mood swings. The Siheyuan’s well was only a shallow prop, so Chen Ge did not fear for the child’s safety. What intrigued him was the boy’s fixation on it.

After another three minutes, the boy reluctantly released the rim, apparently unable to find whatever he sought. He was unlike other children; dark, sinister places made him more animated, not less.

“Since you’re already inside, I suppose a short tour won’t hurt.” Chen Ge focused on the boy, who was small even for his age. Delicate features framed large, ebony-black eyes.

“Minghun is modeled after a traditional Siheyuan. The east and west wings usually housed the younger generations.” He opened the door to the east wing, and a female ghost in bridal robes glided out without warning. The woman screamed and stumbled backward.

“Don’t worry, it’s just an actor.” Chen Ge stopped the bride and whispered, “Xu Wan, go take a break for now.”

“Boss, couldn’t you at least pretend to be scared? What a buzzkill…” Xu Wan gathered her dress and stepped over the wooden threshold. Fan Yu darted around Chen Ge, stopped directly before her, and tilted his head back to study her face.

“Hmm? Boss, why did you let such a young boy inside?” Xu Wan sounded surprised, but only Chen Ge grasped how strange the situation was. In her blood-red bridal gown and Mortician’s Makeup, Xu Wan resembled a corpse. Yet Fan Yu showed no fear. He had eagerly approached for a closer look.

“The kid seems to like me.” Xu Wan smiled at Chen Ge. It was not until Xu Wan left the scenario that the boy pulled his gaze back.

“That’s enough of a tour for today. The rest is decorated much the same way, so let’s head out.” Chen Ge and the woman started toward the exit, but Fan Yu stopped in the courtyard and scanned from side to side as if searching for something.

“Fan Yu, it’s time to go!”

The boy ignored the woman. He moved back to the old well and continued his search.

“Isn’t the boy afraid?” Chen Ge did not rush them but started chatting with the woman. “Are you his mother?”

“No, I’m his aunt. I’m sorry for all the trouble. Xiao Yu is different from other boys his age. He’s been like this since the accident involving his parents several years ago. We’ve taken him to countless doctors, but nothing has helped.”

“Psychological problems? If you don’t mind me asking, what happened to his parents?” Chen Ge asked cautiously.

“Xiao Yu’s parents both taught at Mu Yang High School. One day they disappeared, and no one has found them since. Xiao Yu was only five. I didn’t know how to explain it, so I lied and told him his parents had gone to a faraway place called heaven.”

“Mu Yang High School?!” Chen Ge tensed after hearing these four words.

“You’ve heard of it? That school has always been surrounded by rumors. I urged Xiao Yu’s parents to find work elsewhere, but they wouldn’t listen.” The memory reddened her eyes. She broke off the conversation and approached the boy. “Xiao Yu, it’s time to go home.”

The boy remained stubbornly beside the well, deepening Chen Ge’s curiosity. He crouched next to him. “Why do you keep looking inside? Is there a monster down there?”

Fan Yu shook his head. Sheltered from the sun in the courtyard’s corner, he appeared to have lowered his guard.

“Then can you tell me why you don’t want to leave the well?”

The boy glanced at a spot behind Chen Ge before answering, “I’m looking for something.”

“What are you looking for?” Chen Ge was curious.

The boy looked down the dark well for a long time before answering, “Heaven.”
